title: Content-Aware Adaptive Token Pruning for Video-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.03112v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Vision-language models excel at image and video understanding but suffer from high inference latency due to the need to process thousands of tokens per image, limiting their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices and in real-time surveillance applications. This challenge is further amplified in video processing, where multiple frames must be analyzed simultaneously. Existing token reduction techniques generally rely on a fixed, uniform pruning ratio applied across all inputs, which is suboptimal because the degree of redundancy can vary significantly between different videos, necessitating content-dependent pruning levels to preserve critical information. To address these limitations, we propose an adaptive token pruning strategy specifically designed for video processing. translated_title: 面向视频-语言模型的内容感知自适应Token剪枝
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言模型在图像和视频理解方面表现出色，但由于每张图像需要处理数千个token，导致推理延迟较高，这限制了其在资源受限的边缘设备和实时监控应用中的部署。在视频处理中，由于需要同时分析多帧，这一挑战被进一步放大。现有的token削减技术通常依赖于对所有输入采用固定且统一的剪枝比例，这种方式是次优的，因为不同视频之间的冗余程度可能存在显著差异，需要根据内容确定不同的剪枝级别才能保留关键信息。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了一种专为视频处理设计的自适应token剪枝策略。关键在于，剪枝比例是根据每个视频的内容自适应确定的。这是通过分析（视频token之间的）相关性结构来实现的。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种面向视频-语言模型的内容感知自适应token剪枝策略，能够根据每个视频内容的冗余程度动态确定剪枝比例，在降低推理延迟的同时有效保留关键信息。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a content-aware adaptive token pruning strategy for video-language models that dynamically determines the pruning ratio based on each video's content, reducing inference latency while preserving critical information.
